items.title: On an integral scheme a perfect complex becomes locally free with constant ranks on an open, and of tor dimension at most one after an admissible blowup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a perfect complex E on an integral scheme X the lemma produces a nonempty open U on which every cohomology sheaf H^i(E|_U) is finite locally free of constant rank r_i, together with a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X such that every H^i(Lb^*E) is perfect of tor dimension at most one (statement lines 13105-13113). The proof of the existence of U is genuinely written out despite the author's rhetorical remark: at the generic point eta the complex E becomes a finite complex of finite dimensional vector spaces with zero differentials, with dimensions r_i; the perfect object E' represented by the complex with terms O_X^{r_i} and zero differentials becomes isomorphic to E after pulling back to eta, and the relatively perfect descent lemma then gives an open neighbourhood U of eta on which E and E' agree (proof lines 13116-13127). The blowup assertion is then deduced from the first part and the earlier blowup lemma, using that any nonempty open is scheme theoretically dense in an integral scheme (proof lines 13127-13129). Building the model complex from the dimensions at the generic point and applying relative perfectness to spread it out is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
